cleared.check: Task 1. The clang harness emitter path of monad v0.16.7 was rebuilt from the source cycle 23 fetched, with every monad object compiled fresh, and one hook added to category/vm/compiler/ir/x86.cpp (research/network-risk/cycles/031/theme-monad-gcc-real-states.work/scripts/mkhook.py, src/x86_hook.cpp). The hook writes the virtual stack at entry to each compiled block, before each instruction's emit call and before the terminator's emit call: per element every location (literal, general register, AVX register, stack offset with its PrevLoc), its stack indices and reserve counts, the free general and AVX register queues, the available stack offsets, top_index, min_delta, max_delta, delta, the register owner tables and the deferred comparison. Private members are read through pointers to members, so no access specifier or layout changes. The local x86.cpp, emitter.cpp and virtual_stack.hpp were checked byte-equal to the v0.16.7 tag on GitHub.
cleared.result: The hooked build writes 10,748 states for the 24,009-byte PoolManager runtime and emits a listing of 48,690 lines that equals the unhooked rebuild and the cycle 27 listing used by cycles 28 to 30 (pm-asm-0.16.7.txt) line for line, with 0 differing read-only data bytes once the 22 eight-byte words that hold runtime routine addresses, which ASLR moves between two runs of the same binary, are masked (out/asmcmp.txt). The hook therefore does not change what is emitted. Because compilation emits every block whether or not it runs, the log holds the real compile-time state of every instruction of all 128 un-entered value blocks: 2,138 states over 1,882 instructions (out/value128-ops.json). The runtime on chain 143 equals the compiled runtime byte for byte (eth_getCode at block 0x77f6d37, sha256 288b9772...).

cleared.check: Whole-program compiler dependence of the emitter on the PoolManager. The same emitter, virtual stack, basic block and runtime sources were built a second time with the system gcc 13.3.0 at -O2 -march=haswell (the interpreter object is left out because gcc 13 lacks musttail, and a two-line shim supplies __builtin_addcll and __builtin_subcll, which gcc 13 lacks). The gcc build then compiled the PoolManager with and without the hook.
cleared.result: The gcc 13.3 listing equals the clang 18 listing on all 48,690 lines and all unmasked read-only data bytes, so all 913 compiled blocks, the 128 un-entered value blocks among them, get the same instructions from both compilers. The 10,748 hook states of the gcc build equal those of the clang build once element pointers are renamed (out/statecmp-gcc13.txt). So no unspecified argument evaluation order, implementation-defined behaviour or undefined behaviour in the emitter source resolves differently between clang and gcc on this bytecode. This is gcc 13.3, not the gcc 15.2.0 that built the shipped validator, so it does not exclude a fault introduced by gcc 15.2.0 code generation itself.

cleared.check: Task 2 and 3 for the shift sites of the 128 un-entered value blocks: 9 SHL and 3 SHR, all with a literal count, in blocks 0xf0f, 0x21d0, 0x2806, 0x28f2, 0x2907, 0x5757, 0x57ca, 0x5860 and 0x588a (the FullMath.mulDiv 512-bit blocks 0x5757, 0x57ca, 0x5860, 0x588a among them, src/libraries/FullMath.sol:47-54). The logged state of each site was laid out as the gcc 15.2.0 build reads the Stack (cycle 30 layout, both element vectors, top_index, min_delta, max_delta, available offsets, free queues, reserve counts), and the package's whole Emitter::shl() 0x391590 or Emitter::shr() 0x38d1a0 ran in the x86 model with shift_by_literal 0x372dc0 and 0x374090, Stack::pop, Stack::push and the general register allocator lifted from the package text. The stream was compared with the clang listing body of the same pc, the gcc Stack after the call with the clang hook state of the next instruction, and the stream was run on 2,000 operand sets per site (seed 3131, words 0, 1, 2^256-1, 2^255 and random 64, 128 and 256 bit) against pyevm.py.
cleared.result: All 12 streams equal the clang listing up to consistent renaming (at 0x587d the renaming includes the rcx row of the limb table). At all 12 sites the gcc Stack after the call equals the clang state before the next instruction in every element location, available offset, free register and delta. 24,000 runs gave no wrong result word and no overwritten live operand. Six planted faults were caught: a wrong bit mask in the SHL literal arm (4 sites flagged, 561 wrong runs), a wrong limb index in it (9 sites), a wrong bit mask in the SHR literal arm (1 site), a wrong top index in Stack::push (12 sites, by the state comparison), a stale offset returned by StackElem::free_stack_offset (2 sites, by the state comparison) and a swapped dup source in the input state (12 sites, by the stream comparison). Three cycle 30 faults on the spill and variable-count paths were not flagged because no site reaches those paths: none of the 12 states spills. The caller-saved register and mulmod argument order faults were not planted: no runtime call is on these paths.

cleared.check: Task 5. Whether any word written by a compiled block differs between the gcc model, the clang harness and pyevm.py, and what src/ line would read it.
cleared.result: No block was found where the gcc stream differs from the clang listing beyond renaming, so the Task 3 whole-block runs had no block to run and no word differs. The src lines whose values pass through the sites that ran are the caller shifts by the FixedPoint96.sol:9 and FixedPoint128.sol:7 constants inside the blocks that also hold FullMath.sol:47-54 (the remainder mulmod and the 512-bit subtraction of mulDiv) and the Pool and TickBitmap shifts in blocks 0xf0f to 0x2907. No path for an ordinary account to take or lock funds follows from this unit.

cleared.check: Whether the gcc-built native emitter question applies outside Monad.
cleared.result: It does not. The emitter, its virtual stack and the gcc 15.2.0 validator build are Monad's own (monad v0.16.7). The other 20 networks run interpreters (go-ethereum family, revm family, Nitro, Tempo, mega-evm and the HyperEVM node) that earlier cycles tested and that this unit does not touch.

leadResults.answer: Task 1 is done: the hooked clang harness logs the real virtual stack of every instruction of all 913 compiled blocks and emits exactly the cycle 27 listing. For the 128 un-entered value blocks (1,882 instructions, 2,138 states) the package's gcc 15.2.0 emitter was run on those real states only at the 12 literal-count SHL and SHR sites, among them the FullMath.mulDiv blocks 0x5757, 0x57ca, 0x5860 and 0x588a: every stream equals the clang listing up to renaming, every post-call Stack state equals the clang one, 24,000 operand runs match pyevm.py, and six planted faults are caught. A system gcc 13.3 rebuild of the same source gives the identical listing and identical states for all blocks. The remaining emit functions, listed per block in out/task4.json, have not been run from the package on real states, so the lead is not closed. No word that differs was found, and nothing here gives an ordinary account a way to take or lock funds on chain 143 or on the other 20 networks.
